name: Marketplace enforcement metrics require an explicit non-DPRK denominator

attribution.legal_posture: This is first-party platform-control or threat-research guidance normalized as defensive context; identity attribution and control effectiveness require separate evidence.

caveats: Marketplace-wide abuse-enforcement metrics describe platform activity; confirmed DPRK accounts, workers, applications, and hires require separate sourcing.
Metrics cover all marketplace abuse rather than DPRK-specific activity; they measure marketplace reports, with undetected accounts and successful fraudulent hires outside scope.

statements: Upwork reported that malicious-client offers declined more than 91% year over year, bad-actor freelancer proposals fell 82%, identity-verified freelancers increased 22%, and LLM-assisted moderation with human review caught nearly 40,000 violating jobs not detected by other models or reports.
limitations: Metrics cover all marketplace abuse and are not DPRK-specific. They do not measure undetected accounts or successful fraudulent hires.

sources.support: Upwork reports marketplace-wide 2025 enforcement changes, including lower malicious-client offers and bad-actor freelancer proposals and nearly 40,000 violating jobs found by LLM-assisted moderation with human review. These are all-abuse metrics, not confirmed DPRK-worker counts or a measure of successful hires
sources.locator: PDF pp. 2-5, especially p. 4 'Our progress in 2025'
